title: Old-Time Rag Doll Seed Test
subtitle: Check Old Seeds Before Spring
items: Roll 10 seeds in a damp cloth
Sow thicker if rate is low
intro: Old USDA Farmers' Bulletins urged farmers to test seed before planting, and the 'rag doll' test is the simplest way. A damp cloth, ten seeds and a week of patience tell you whether last year's packets are still worth sowing.
desc: Old-time rag doll seed germination test: roll 10 seeds in a damp cloth, keep it warm, count the sprouts after a week and know if old seed packets are still good before spring planting. A thrifty homestead trick. Full list on the blog.

title: How to Can Crushed Tomatoes
subtitle: Water Bath, Step by Step
items: Quarter and crush as you heat
intro: Crushed tomatoes are one of the most useful jars in a winter pantry, and frozen garden tomatoes work too. This follows the tested hot-pack method from the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: bottled lemon juice in every jar is not optional.
desc: How to can crushed tomatoes in a water bath canner: peel, crush and boil 5 minutes, add bottled lemon juice to every jar, leave 1/2 inch headspace and process pints 35 minutes, quarts 45. Safe, tested home canning steps. Full list on the blog.

title: Winterize Your Garden Hose
subtitle: Before the Hard Freeze
items: Unhook it before a hard freeze
Drain it fully, end to end
Shut off and drain the spigot
desc: How to winterize a garden hose: disconnect before a hard freeze, drain it end to end, coil it loosely and store it indoors, then shut off and drain the outdoor spigot. Simple winter garden tool care for beginners. (Contains affiliate links.)

title: How to Dry Onions at Home
subtitle: Flakes and Powder for Winter
items: Dry in a garage, it's strong
intro: Dried onion flakes take up a fraction of the space of fresh onions and keep for many months in a dark cupboard. Old USDA bulletins on drying vegetables used the same basics: thin, even slices, steady low heat and good airflow.
desc: How to dry onions in a dehydrator or oven: slice evenly, dry at 130-140°F until brittle, then store the flakes airtight or grind them into homemade onion powder. Easy food preservation for a winter pantry. Full list on the blog.

title: Grow Lettuce Indoors in Winter
subtitle: Fresh Salad on the Windowsill
items: Water when top inch is dry
intro: Loose-leaf lettuce is one of the easiest vegetables to grow indoors over winter. A shallow pot, a bright window or a simple grow light, and cool room temperatures give you cut-and-come-again salads until spring.
desc: How to grow lettuce indoors in winter: choose loose-leaf varieties, sow 1/8 inch deep in a 6-inch pot, keep it cool and give 14-16 hours of light, then harvest outer leaves again and again. Easy indoor vegetable garden for beginners. Full list on the blog.

title: How to Make Butter at Home
subtitle: An Old Farm Kitchen Skill
items: Shake or mix until it breaks
Rinse in ice water till clear
Press out every bit of water
intro: Churning butter was a weekly chore on old farms, and it still takes only a jar or a mixer and some patience. Washing out the buttermilk is the step people skip, and it is what keeps homemade butter from going sour fast.
desc: How to make homemade butter from heavy cream: shake or mix until it breaks, save the buttermilk, rinse the butter in ice water and press out the water so it keeps longer. A simple self-sufficient kitchen skill. Full list on the blog.
